newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Lightning knocks out Johannesburg airport radar.
newsitem.headline: Lightning knocks out Johannesburg airport radar.

text.p: A bolt of lightning struck Johannesburg airport control tower during a very violent storm, knocking out all four radar antennae for the first time and delaying traffic, officials said on Wednesday.
"We've got the antennae turning again and hope to be back to normal by lunchtime," said air traffic control spokesman Arthur Bradshaw.
Flights were being kept 10 minutes apart from each other for safety -- much further than the five nautical mile gap allowed when the radars operate -- and this was causing delays.
The intense electrical storm lashed South Africa's commercial capital on Tuesday night, startling even residents used to nightly summer tempests.
Bradshaw said it was the first time that lightning had ever knocked out all the airport's radars at once.
"You can put in as much lightning protection as you like but the lightning can find a way to get in," he said.
"It appears it came in from the bottom so all the protection at the top was to no avail."
